title: Remote Screening and Navigation to Increase Trial Enrollment, INVITE Trial
official: INVITE: Remote ScreenIng & NaVigation to Increase Trial Enrollment
summary: This clinical trial studies the feasibility, acceptability, appropriateness, and effectiveness of a remote screening and navigation program in increasing clinical trial enrollment among patients with prostate and bladder cancer receiving cancer care in the community setting. Genitourinary (GU) cancers, including prostate and bladder cancer, are among the most common affecting patients in the United States. In spite of recent advances, there are still only a few broad categories of treatments effective in both prostate and bladder cancer, and investigating new therapies in clinical trials is essential. In Washington State, the majority of patients with prostate and bladder cancer are treated at local community oncology sites. Patients are referred to Fred Hutch (FH) GU oncologists for clinical trials, but often this referral occurs once a patient has exhausted all standard of care options for treatment. This remote screening and navigation study involves approaching patients at community oncology and urology clinics in the Washington State area and pre-screening them for eligibility in open clinical trials at FH. Interested eligible patients will then be referred to our patient navigation program to be seen by a GU medical oncologist at Fred Hutch Cancer Center. This program may help increase access to clinical trials for patients with prostate and bladder cancer, as well as strengthen collaboration between community oncology providers and GU oncology specialists at FH.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥ 18
* Ability to understand English or Spanish
* Records must be available to review on Epic CareEverywhere
* Ability to understand and willingness to sign a written informed consent document. Legally authorized representatives (LAR) may sign and give informed consent on behalf of study participants

  * For participants utilizing LAR, participant must assent or otherwise be capable of completing patient-reported surveys
* Receiving care for prostate or bladder cancer at participating community sites
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (PS) 0-3
* Not enrolled in hospice

sites.f: Fred Hutch/University of Washington Cancer Consortium
